text:
Maria S.: quick heads-up — the sampleapp e2e load test produced duplicated invoices when token rotation hit mid-run and we had a very small jitter (0-5ms). Repro is fairly consistent.
Alex K.: ugh. can you paste the minimal repro steps? is the SDK attaching idempotency keys or are we relying on app to set them?
Maria S.: steps:
  1) run load script `scripts/load-invoices.sh --users 200 --rate 50`
  2) trigger token rotation via auth service (rotate/refresh)
  3) observe a flurry of 429s then retries
Logs:
```
WARN 2026-03-22T12:01:02Z request_retry: got 429, retrying attempt=1 idempotency_key=invoice-create-usr42
INFO 2026-03-22T12:01:02Z sdk_retry backoff=0.004 jitter=0.003 token=rotating
WARN 2026-03-22T12:01:02Z request_retry: got 429, retrying attempt=2 idempotency_key=invoice-create-usr42
ERROR 2026-03-22T12:01:02Z invoice_service: duplicate detected later but already created
```
Maria S.: SDK currently does not auto-generate idempotency keys for create endpoints in sampleapp; we were expecting app-level idempotency but with unsafe replay window + tiny jitter we ended up replaying twice.
Ryan P.: sounds like two problems: 1) sampleapp relying on app-supplied idempotency without enforcing uniqueness, 2) jitter window too small -> synchronization during token refresh creates retry storms. my recs:
  - sampleapp: include an `Idempotency-Key` by default for resource-create calls. e.g. `Idempotency-Key: invoice-<user>-<timestamp>-<rand8>`
  - SDK: expose `retry.jitter = full|equal|none` and set default to `full` for hosted envs
  - instrumentation: emit `duplicate_count` and `replay_window_ms` to detect regressions
Alex K.: agreed. For patch i'm gonna: (a) default sampleapp create endpoints to attach `Idempotency-Key` when not provided, (b) add short-lived client-side monotonic counter to the key for safe replays, (c) add unit/integration test that simulates token rotation + 429s.
Maria S.: is there a consensus on jitter algorithm? i'd prefer `full-jitter` for edge cases like auth rotation.
Ryan P.: full-jitter usually wins for bursty failures. equal/jitter variants are fine for predictable latencies but not for auth storming. also recommend cap on max_retries when token is rotating + backoff to 1s/2s quickly.
Alex K.: PR in a sec: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sampleapp/pull/842 (WIP) — will add `Idempotency-Key` header + test harness. also toggling SDK default to `full` via env `REDWOOD_SDK_RETRY_JITTER=full` in sampleapp configs.
DeployBot: deploy/sampleapp-loadtest v2.14.1 started by Alex K. — status: pending
Maria S.: one more ask — can we add a debug flag that logs `X-Idempotency-Key` per attempt in dev only? helps QA reproduce dupes.
Alex K.: will add `--debug-idempotency` flag to the load runner and an extra `X-Debug-Idempotency: true` header.
Ryan P.: ack. after PR review i'll run the load test and post metrics. thanks folks :thumbsup:)
